# Eurovision Song Contest winners — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/eurovision-winners.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/eurovision-winners.ttl`](../decks/eurovision-winners.ttl) · **Cards:** 70 · **Licence:** [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

The winners of every Eurovision Song Contest from the first, in 1956, to the 70th, in May 2026: 70 cards (no contest was held in 2020). Front: the contest, e.g. “Eurovision Song Contest 1974”; back: the winning country and song, e.g. Sweden – “Waterloo”, with the performer in a note. Song titles are given as performed, untranslated. The 1969 contest ended in a four-way tie, so its card names all four winners. Taken from Wikidata and the English Wikipedia and checked against the EBU’s eurovision.com and the Swedish Wikipedia.

## Licensing

The content sources are Wikidata (CC0) and the English Wikipedia list of winners (CC BY-SA 4.0). Wikidata gives the contests, the winning entries of 1956–2025, their titles, performers and countries and the English and Swedish names. Wikidata does not record the result of the 2026 contest, and no openly licensed (CC0, public domain or CC BY) report of the 2026 result was found (Wikinews has none); these facts, some credited performer names and two corrected titles were taken from the English Wikipedia list, which makes the deck CC BY-SA 4.0, with the list attributed in the deck (prov:wasDerivedFrom) and in this report. No wording or table layout was copied from it: the cards are the compiler's own phrasing of facts. The selection is the complete set of contests held, which every list of winners shares, not a choice taken from one. eurovision.com (EBU, all rights reserved), the BTA report (all rights reserved) and the Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only: they confirmed facts that the content sources gave, and nothing was copied from them. If Wikidata comes to record the 2026 winner, and the credited names and titles listed under the English Wikipedia source can be confirmed from openly licensed data, the deck could be rebuilt without the English Wikipedia list and released as CC0.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. 1. Contests (Wikidata, query 2): every item that is part of the series Eurovision Song Contest (P179 Q276) with a P1545 ordinal, its date (P585), its English, Swedish and multilingual labels and its winner statements (P1346 with their P1532 and P175 qualifiers), fetched as CSV from the Wikidata Query Service. Ordinals 1 to 70 run from 1956 to 2026; the cancelled 2020 contest (Q30973589) has no ordinal and no winner, and the items for 2027–2029 are future contests. The edition items' P1346 statements are inconsistent: for 1956–1960 and 2004–2025 most name the performer rather than the song, and 2026 has none. (Query 1, which looked for editions as instances of Q276, returned nothing: Q276 is the series, the editions are instances of Q110288240.)
3. 2. Winning entries (Wikidata, query 3 and entries.py): every item with P2522 (victory) = an edition, or a P1344 (participant in) statement for an edition with the qualifier P1352 (ranking) 1. The result mixes the entry items (instances of Q63481999, Eurovision Song Contest entry), song items and performer items; for each contest the entry item was chosen (for 2007, which has none, the song item “Molitva”, Q753818), and the chosen items were fetched in full with the Wikidata API (wbgetentities) by entries.py, with the items they name. 1969 has four entry items with ranking 1. The card's title is the entry's English label; its country is the P17 qualifier of its P1344 statement, or where there is none the P1532 (country for sport) qualifier of the edition's P1346 statement (1965, 1974, 1995, 2013, 2015) or, for 2007, its P1268 (represents) qualifier Serbia (Q10153's P1346 names the performer Marija Šerifović, with the qualifiers P1686 (for work) Molitva and P1268 Serbia; query 2 did not ask for P1268, and the qualifier was read with wbgetclaims, query 10); for 2025 the item Austria in the Eurovision Song Contest 2025 (Q131936274: P17 Austria, P175 JJ), found by country_items.py.
4. 3. 2026: the Wikidata item of the 70th contest (Q125933843, last modified 2026-09-27) records no winner, and none of the 75 items with P1344 = Q125933843 (found with the search haswbstatement:P1344=Q125933843, entries2026.py) carries a ranking. The result was therefore established from sources fetched on the day of research: a web search, the contest page and the final scoreboard on eurovision.com (Bulgaria, DARA, “Bangaranga”, 516 points), the English and Swedish Wikipedia lists of winners, and the Bulgarian News Agency's report (“Dara's song, Bangaranga, collected 516 points and secured Bulgaria's first ever win”). The English Wikipedia list is the content source for this fact; the song item Q138666487 in Wikidata gives its title, performer (Dara, Q27643209) and country (P17 and P495 Bulgaria).
5. 4. Independent check, the organiser (eurovision.com): the URL of every contest page was taken from the edition items' P856 (query 5); the eurovision.tv/event/ addresses that Wikidata gives for 1979 and 1981–1999 answered 403 and were replaced by the same page on eurovision.com. fetch_ebu.py downloaded each page and read the three lines after each “Winner” heading (performer, song, country); fetch_finals.py followed each page's link to its (grand) final and read every entry in place 1 of the scoreboard (points, country, performer, song). The contest pages of 2012, 2016, 2018, 2019, 2023 and 2024 have no “Winner” box and the final pages of 1959 and 1970 no scoreboard; every contest is covered by at least one of the two.
6. 5. Independent check, the encyclopaedias: the English list “List of Eurovision Song Contest winners” (revision 1370224646) and the Swedish list “Lista över vinnare i Eurovision Song Contest” (revision 59337108) were fetched with their revision ids through the MediaWiki API (query 7) and their winners tables parsed by parse_wiki.py (country, song, performer; in Swedish also the language).
7. 6. Comparison: compare.py compared, for every contest, the winning country and the song title (case, punctuation and spaces ignored) in Wikidata, on both eurovision.com pages and in both Wikipedia lists, through a fixed table of each source's country names. All four agree on the winning country and song of all 70 contests, apart from the errors and gaps listed under quality control round 0 (Wikidata's France for 1961 and 1973, its “Belive” for 2008, two typing errors in the Swedish list, the countries Wikidata does not tie to an entry). The evidence on every card (the “says” texts) was generated by make_cards.py from the parsed source files, not typed by hand, except the Swedish Wikipedia row for 2026, whose year cell the parser did not recognise and which was read by hand. The scripts are not published with the deck; the rules above are what they do.
8. 7. Card text. Front: the contest's name, which is the same in English and Swedish (the Wikidata en and sv labels — for 2026, which has no Swedish label, the multilingual (mul) label, which the builder's sv check also accepts — and the titles of the Swedish Wikipedia articles, e.g. “Eurovision Song Contest 1974”). Back: the country, an en dash and the song title in quotation marks (English “…”, Swedish ”…”); in 1969 the four entries in alphabetical order of the English country names, which is also the Swedish order. The country is named as it was at the time (West Germany 1982, Yugoslavia 1989), in English and Swedish from the Wikidata labels; Yugoslavia's Wikidata label is the full name of the state, so the cards use its English alias “Yugoslavia” and the Swedish “Jugoslavien”, the Swedish label of Wikidata's item Yugoslavia (Q36704). The song title is the title as performed, in its own language and untranslated, written as Wikidata's English label of the entry gives it except where that label is wrong (1984, 2008; see quality control), and with the typographic apostrophe ’ where the label has the straight one (1964, 1977, 1980, 1986, 1994; the label checks compare against the label as Wikidata writes it). A back is therefore an English or Swedish phrase that quotes a title which may be in another language (French, Dutch, Italian, Hebrew, German, Norwegian, Swedish, Serbian, Portuguese, Ukrainian, or an invented word): the whole back is tagged en and sv, and the quoted title is a name, not text in that language. Note: the performer as credited at the contest, in the form most sources share (eurovision.com, the English Wikipedia list and Wikidata's performer labels and aliases); for 1979, where eurovision.com credits “Milk & Honey with Gali Atari” and the English list only “Milk and Honey”, the note follows Wikidata's alias “Gali Atari & Milk and Honey” of Q926040. “Performed by …” / “Framförd av …”, with “and” or “&” rendered “och” in Swedish where it joins names (not inside a band's name such as Milk and Honey; “Grethe och Jørgen Ingmann” is also a Swedish alias of Q241520). In 1978 the English credit “Izhar Cohen and the Alphabeta” keeps the English article; Swedish has no such article before a band's name, so the Swedish note names the band Alphabeta, its Wikidata label (Q661126). ABBA is written Abba in Swedish, the Wikidata sv label of Q18233. The Swedish Wikipedia list was used only to confirm these forms.
9. 8. Machine checks: every card's checks (run against live Wikidata by the deck builder) confirm the English and Swedish labels of the contest (for 2026 the multilingual label, there being no sv label), that the winning entry's item participated in that contest (P1344) or won it (P2522, victory), as the item states it, its performer (P175), its English label where it is the card's title, the English and Swedish labels of the country, the Wikidata labels or aliases that the Swedish name forms and the 1963, 1978 and 1979 credits rest on, and, where Wikidata states it, that the contest's P1346 (winner) is the entry. The checks cannot test qualifiers, so the ranking 1 and the country qualifiers are covered by the evidence and the comparison of step 6, not by the builder; the 2026 result is not in Wikidata at all.

## Selection

Every Eurovision Song Contest held, from the first (Lugano, 1956) to the 70th (Vienna, May 2026), as of 4 October 2026: 70 cards, one per contest. The 2020 contest was cancelled (COVID-19 pandemic) and has no winner and no card. The 1969 contest ended in a tie between four entries on 18 points each (France, the Netherlands, Spain and the United Kingdom), all of which are listed as winners by the EBU, Wikidata and both Wikipedias; its card names all four. Left out: runners-up and points (except the 18 points of the 1969 tie, in its note), the host cities, the songwriters, the languages of the songs, the national selections (such as Melodifestivalen) and other Eurovision events (Junior Eurovision, Eurovision Song Contest Asia). The 2027 contest has not been held; the 2026 card is the cut-off.

## Queries

**1. First attempt: editions as instances of Q276 (returned no rows; Q276 is the series) (sh <scratch>/run.sh q1, which runs: curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@<scratch>/q1.rq https://query.wikidata.org/sparql > <scratch>/q1.csv)** (Wikidata: the editions of the Eurovision Song Contest (series Q276), their winners (P1346) and the winning entries' participation (P1344 with ranking P1352 and country P17), victory (P2522), performers (P175) and English and Swedish labels)

```
SELECT ?edition ?editionLabelEn ?editionLabelSv ?year ?winner ?winnerLabelEn ?winnerType WHERE {
  ?edition wdt:P31 wd:Q276 .
  OPTIONAL { ?edition wdt:P585 ?date . BIND(YEAR(?date) AS ?year) }
  OPTIONAL { ?edition wdt:P1346 ?winner .
    OPTIONAL { ?winner rdfs:label ?winnerLabelEn FILTER(LANG(?winnerLabelEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?winner wdt:P31 ?winnerType } }
  OPTIONAL { ?edition rdfs:label ?editionLabelEn FILTER(LANG(?editionLabelEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?edition rdfs:label ?editionLabelSv FILTER(LANG(?editionLabelSv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?year

```

**2. Every contest in the series Q276 with its ordinal, date, labels and P1346 winner statements (with their P1532 and P175 qualifiers only; the 2007 statement's P1268 (represents) qualifier was read with query 10) (sh <scratch>/run.sh q2)** (Wikidata: the editions of the Eurovision Song Contest (series Q276), their winners (P1346) and the winning entries' participation (P1344 with ranking P1352 and country P17), victory (P2522), performers (P175) and English and Swedish labels)

```
SELECT ?edition ?ordinal ?year ?editionEn ?editionSv ?editionMul ?song ?songEn ?songMul ?songSv ?country ?countryEn ?countrySv ?performer ?performerEn ?performerMul ?performerSv ?rank WHERE {
  ?edition p:P179 ?ser .
  ?ser ps:P179 wd:Q276 .
  OPTIONAL { ?ser pq:P1545 ?ordinal }
  OPTIONAL { ?edition wdt:P585 ?date . BIND(YEAR(?date) AS ?year) }
  OPTIONAL { ?edition rdfs:label ?editionEn FILTER(LANG(?editionEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?edition rdfs:label ?editionSv FILTER(LANG(?editionSv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?edition rdfs:label ?editionMul FILTER(LANG(?editionMul) = "mul") }
  OPTIONAL {
    ?edition p:P1346 ?w .
    ?w ps:P1346 ?song ; wikibase:rank ?rank .
    OPTIONAL { ?song rdfs:label ?songEn FILTER(LANG(?songEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?song rdfs:label ?songMul FILTER(LANG(?songMul) = "mul") }
    OPTIONAL { ?song rdfs:label ?songSv FILTER(LANG(?songSv) = "sv") }
    OPTIONAL { ?w pq:P1532 ?country .
      OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countryEn FILTER(LANG(?countryEn) = "en") }
      OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countrySv FILTER(LANG(?countrySv) = "sv") } }
    OPTIONAL { ?w pq:P175 ?performer .
      OPTIONAL { ?performer rdfs:label ?performerEn FILTER(LANG(?performerEn) = "en") }
      OPTIONAL { ?performer rdfs:label ?performerMul FILTER(LANG(?performerMul) = "mul") }
      OPTIONAL { ?performer rdfs:label ?performerSv FILTER(LANG(?performerSv) = "sv") } }
  }
}
ORDER BY xsd:integer(?ordinal)

```

**3. Items that won a contest (P2522) or were ranked 1st in it (P1344 with P1352 = 1), with title, country and performer (sh <scratch>/run.sh q3)** (Wikidata: the editions of the Eurovision Song Contest (series Q276), their winners (P1346) and the winning entries' participation (P1344 with ranking P1352 and country P17), victory (P2522), performers (P175) and English and Swedish labels)

```
SELECT ?edition ?year ?entry ?entryEn ?title ?titleLang ?rank1 ?country ?countryEn ?countrySv ?performer ?performerEn ?performerMul ?performerSv ?entryType WHERE {
  ?edition p:P179/ps:P179 wd:Q276 ; wdt:P585 ?date .
  BIND(YEAR(?date) AS ?year)
  { ?entry wdt:P2522 ?edition } UNION
  { ?entry p:P1344 ?part . ?part ps:P1344 ?edition ; pq:P1352 ?rank1 . FILTER(?rank1 = 1) }
  OPTIONAL { ?entry wdt:P31 ?entryType }
  OPTIONAL { ?entry rdfs:label ?entryEn FILTER(LANG(?entryEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?entry wdt:P1476 ?title . BIND(LANG(?title) AS ?titleLang) }
  OPTIONAL { ?entry p:P1344 ?p2 . ?p2 ps:P1344 ?edition .
    OPTIONAL { ?p2 pq:P17 ?country .
      OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countryEn FILTER(LANG(?countryEn) = "en") }
      OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countrySv FILTER(LANG(?countrySv) = "sv") } } }
  OPTIONAL { ?entry wdt:P175 ?performer .
    OPTIONAL { ?performer rdfs:label ?performerEn FILTER(LANG(?performerEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?performer rdfs:label ?performerMul FILTER(LANG(?performerMul) = "mul") }
    OPTIONAL { ?performer rdfs:label ?performerSv FILTER(LANG(?performerSv) = "sv") } }
}
ORDER BY ?year

```

curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" "https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:EntityData/Q125933843.json" -o <scratch>/Q125933843.json

The official website (P856) of every contest (sh <scratch>/run.sh q5)** (Wikidata: the editions of the Eurovision Song Contest (series Q276), their winners (P1346) and the winning entries' participation (P1344 with ranking P1352 and country P17), victory (P2522), performers (P175) and English and Swedish labels)

## Quality control

5 rounds, 27 findings: 15 fixed, 2 rejected after checking, 10 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (608 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's winning country and song in Wikidata, on eurovision.com (contest page and final scoreboard) and in the English and Swedish Wikipedia lists; the 2026 result against sources fetched on the day; the Swedish names against the Wikidata sv labels and the Swedish list. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 70 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.

The four sources agree on the winning country and song of every contest from 1956 to 2026. Wikidata has two wrong countries, one misspelt title, one wrong title spelling and no 2026 result; the Swedish list has two typing errors; the sources differ in the capitalisation and punctuation of some titles and in the name of the 1982 winning country. Two Wikidata checks were left out (the titles of 1984 and 2008, where the label is wrong); no other check was skipped.

No factual errors. Every card's winning country and song matched the contest's English Wikipedia article except 1982, where the card deliberately says West Germany.
